Trail Physics · Unit 3: Forces & Cornering · Module 7

Newton’s Laws of Motion

Force, mass and inertia; Newton’s three laws; net force and free-body diagrams.

Lesson coming

The question

Why does a heavier bike and rider take more force to get up to speed?

The physics

  • Force and mass
  • Inertia
  • Newton’s first, second and third laws
  • Net force
  • Balanced and unbalanced forces
  • Action and reaction

The math

  • F_net = ma

Learning objectives

  • Explain inertia and Newton’s first law
  • Combine forces to find the net force
  • Use F_net = ma to find a force, mass or acceleration
  • Identify action-reaction pairs, such as tire and trail
  • Draw a free-body diagram for a rider and bike

Helps to know first: Motion in One Dimension, Vectors.

The mountain biking connection

Pedalling pushes the bike forward, braking slows it, and the trail pushes back on the tires. Every change in a rider’s motion comes from an unbalanced force.
